content.explanation:
• Beginner-friendly explanation.
• Neural Networks don't have eyes.

content.title: Image to Tensors
content.explanation: This is the core secret of Computer Vision. The model doesn't see a 'dog', it sees a massive grid of brightness values ranging from 0 (black) to 255 (white).

content.title: The Anatomy of a Perceptron
content.explanation:
• Beginner-friendly explanation.
• The Perceptron is the artificial equivalent of a biological neuron in your brain.
• It is the fundamental building block of Deep Learning.
• Real-world intuition.
• Imagine deciding whether to go out in the rain.

content.title: Neural Network Architecture
content.explanation: A Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) consists of an input layer, hidden layers, and an output layer. Each connection has a learnable weight, allowing the network to approximate any mathematical function.

content.title: Activation Functions: Injecting Reality
content.explanation:
• Beginner-friendly explanation.
• Activation functions are the 'decision makers' at the end of every perceptron.
• Real-world intuition.

• A linear math function is just a straight wire—whatever electricity comes in, goes out.

content.title: Activation Functions in Code
content.explanation:
• Neural Networks rely on Activation Functions to introduce non-linearity.
• Without them, a neural network is just a giant linear regression model!
• The most popular activation function is ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit).
• Mathematically, it's incredibly simple: - If the input is less than 0, return 0.
• - If the input is greater than 0, return the input.

content.title: MLP Architecture Fundamentals

challenge.explanation: This code demonstrates how data flows through an MLP. The tanh activation introduces non-linearity in hidden layers, while softmax converts raw outputs to probability distributions for classification tasks.
challenge.hint: Use tanh for hidden layer activation and softmax for output layer
challenge.question: Implement forward propagation for a 2-layer MLP
challenge.solution:
import numpy as np

def forward_prop(X, W1, b1, W2, b2):
    hidden = np.tanh(X @ W1 + b1)  # First layer with tanh activation
    output = np.softmax(hidden @ W2 + b2, axis=1)  # Output with softmax
    return output
